calibration_anchor.closest_anchor: Market-matching promotional offer with no data, exclusivity, or story angle
calibration_anchor.why_not_higher: A 4.00% APY CD matching what competitors are already advertising is not news; it is marketing
calibration_anchor.why_not_lower: The product is real, but it is a commodity offer

beat_relevance.rationale: Personal-finance beat covers rates, but only when there is new data or differentiation

timeliness.rationale: No news hook, embargo, or external catalyst; only the bank's decision to advertise

magnitude.rationale: A single mid-size bank adjusting its CD rate to match the market has no scale

proof_points.rationale: No exclusive data, market analysis, or comparison provided; just a feature announcement

narrative_quality.rationale: The framing is purely promotional; no consumer story, trend, or conflict

source_credibility.rationale: A mid-size retail bank is a reasonable source on its own products, but lacks uniqueness or insight

improvement_suggestions: Do not pitch this as a news story
If CD rates are shifting due to Fed policy, tie the pitch to the macro event with original data (e.g., first-mover on a major rate drop or exclusive customer research)
evidence_gaps: Exclusive data on customer demand shifts
First-mover advantage or differentiated rate tier
dimensions.honest_assessment: A mid-size bank advertising market-rate CDs is promotional material, not news. Personal-finance reporters see dozens of these pitches per week. Without exclusive data or a clear external story hook, this will not get coverage.

next_move.rationale: Hold until there is a real news angle (e.g., a Fed rate cut, exclusive customer data, or a major competitive differentiation)
